sources.title: Reflecting & Listening Skills
sources.quote: Counselors often go beyond simple repetition and include their own interpretations of the client's emotions or existential meaning to increase the "depth" of the session.
sources.technique: Move beyond reflecting content alone by tentatively connecting what the person said with their feelings or the meaning it may hold for them.

sources.title: Reflective Listening
sources.quote: A reflection seeks to summarize what the person means; it makes a guess.
sources.technique: Offer a concise reflective statement that makes a curious, tentative guess about the speaker’s meaning rather than turning every response into a question.

sources.title: Discussion 3 – Basic Social Work Interviewing Skills and Techniques: A Workbook for Application
sources.quote: Summarizing ... [creates] a consolidated response. This can incorporate both reflections of feeling and content.
sources.technique: When the conversation needs to progress, pull together its main points and feelings in a brief summary instead of asking the person to repeat details already shared.

sources.title: Leader’s Guide: Motivating Clients for Treatment and Addressing Resistance
sources.quote: even the best open questions can begin to feel like “Motivational Interrogation” ... So be sure to balance these with lots of reflections
sources.technique: Balance open questions with reflections so the exchange does not become an interrogation; use reflections to follow the person’s train of thought.
